content:
maria: Heads up — we're seeing p95 token latency SLO misses on us-east-1 / gpu-pool-7 starting ~21:40 UTC. Pattern looks like sustained batching pressure, lots of max_batch rejections.

Dave: Any logs or examples?

maria: Pasted a snippet from the admission controller and runtime: 
```
[2026-02-12T21:40:03Z] pod=gpu-pool-7/shard-12 admission=reject reason=max_batch_exceeded max_batch=32 req_batch=40 queue_time_ms=1208
[2026-02-12T21:40:03Z] pod=gpu-pool-7/shard-12 runtime: start_infer seq_len=1024 tokens=900 mem_peak=12.1GB
[2026-02-12T21:40:07Z] pod=gpu-pool-7/shard-12 admission=accept batch_size=8 packed=true
```

shez: This feels like continuous arrival at 90-95% capacity. Max-batch 32 is optimistic for mixed seq lengths — packing/eviction heuristics are thrashing.

maria: Agree. Also seeing long queue_time_ms spikes that push request latency over SLO, even when individual inferences are fine once scheduled.

runtime-bot: alert: latency_slo_miss count=36 window=5m region=us-east-1 pool=gpu-pool-7

oncall-nick: Quick root-cause hypothesis: admission controller uses static max_batch per-pool. With heavy small-request traffic we get large batches that include occasional long-seq requests; KV cache + mem pressure forces kernel fallbacks and increases per-token time.

dave: Proposed mitigations:
- dynamic per-shard max_batch based on recent seq length distribution
- soft-eviction: don't pack >X% of long-seq into a batch if it causes mean mem > threshold
- tenant-level pacing to avoid one noisy tenant filling the queue

shez: +1. We should also consider temporarily lowering max_batch on the most impacted shards to reduce tail latency. Lower batch -> less packing win but fewer stragglers.

maria: Can we try a canary: set max_batch=24 on 2 shards in gpu-pool-7, and enable per-shard seq_hist tracking flag? CLI: `rwctl runtime update-shard --shard shard-12 --admission.max_batch 24 --admission.track_seq_hist true`

sre-elaine: If we change admission aggressively watch p50/p95/p99. Lowering max_batch may increase cost/tokens due to fewer packing wins — call it out to finance if we roll cluster-wide.

runtime-bot: deploy job started: change-admission-shard-12 by maria at 21:52 UTC

maria: Canary rolled to shard-12 and shard-15 at 21:54 UTC. Monitoring dashboards: https://console.redwood/metrics/gpu-pool-7

dave: Early signals after 5m: queue_time_ms p95 down ~420ms -> 180ms; p99 unchanged yet. p50 slightly up ~10ms.

oncall-nick: Good. Next step: add admission rule to deprioritize requests with seq_len > 800 when arrival rate > 0.85*capacity — effectively give small requests priority so batches finish faster. Pseudoconfig: 
```
admission:
  adaptive_max_batch: true
  long_seq_threshold: 800
  long_seq_deprioritize: true
  deprio_trigger_util: 0.85
```

sre-elaine: Runbook: if p99 increases after canary revert with `rwctl runtime rollback-shard --shard shard-12` and notify infra-pager.

maria: Created ticket INFRA-4893 with experiment details and cost estimate. Linking here: https://tickets.redwood/INFRA-4893 (internal).

dave: Follow-up: we should also surface packing hit-rate and kernel-fallback counts in the latency SLO dashboard so product teams can see the trade-offs.

shez: Agreed. I'll add packing_hit_rate, kernel_fallbacks, seq_hist_percentiles to the runtime metrics.

maria: OK leaving canary running for 30m, if stable we'll expand to 20% of pool and then evaluate cost delta. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
